title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 4th Congressional District
area: Central New Jersey's Ocean and Monmouth counties, including Toms River, Brick, Jackson, and the Jersey Shore from Point Pleasant to Bay Head.

context.text: Incumbent Chris Smith ran unopposed in the June 2, 2026 Republican primary. Rachel Peace won a two-way Democratic primary with 72.8% of the vote (20,782 votes) over John Blake (27.2%).

Cook Political Report rated the district's Partisan Voter Index as R+14 as of September 2026; Donald Trump won the district 64.4%–34.3% under the current district lines in the 2024 presidential election.

candidates.name: Chris Smith
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the June 2 Republican primary
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 4th Congressional District (since 1981); Chair, Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Africa

summary.text: Chris Smith is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 4th District, first elected in 1980 after working in his family's sporting goods business and as executive director of the New Jersey Right to Life Committee. He is a senior member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, chairs its Africa subcommittee, and, according to his House biography, has authored 68 enacted laws, including on human trafficking, autism research, and veterans.

background.text: Born in Rahway, New Jersey, in 1953 and, according to his House biography, grew up in Iselin.
Earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from Trenton State College (now The College of New Jersey) in 1975, and spent a semester abroad at Worcester College in England.

Worked as Director of Institutional Sales at his family-owned sporting goods company and served as Executive Director of the New Jersey Right to Life Committee; Ballotpedia also lists work on political campaigns for Democratic officials.
Ran for Congress as a Republican in 1978 and lost to Rep. Frank Thompson, then defeated Thompson in 1980 to win the seat; he took office in 1981.
Is serving his 23rd term; in the 119th Congress he is a senior member of the Foreign Affairs Committee and chairs its Africa subcommittee, and also sits on its Western Hemisphere subcommittee.

Co-chairs the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission and the Congressional-Executive Commission on China, has served as Special Representative on Human Trafficking for the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly, and has chaired the Helsinki Commission (CSCE) five times.

Chaired the House Veterans' Affairs Committee for two terms, beginning in January 2001, and earlier chaired Foreign Affairs subcommittees on human rights, international operations and organizations, and global health.
Is the author of the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000 and of several autism research laws, among the 68 laws his House biography credits to him.

Chairs or co-founded several bipartisan congressional caucuses, including the Pro-life, Autism, Alzheimer's, Lyme Disease, and Human Trafficking caucuses. According to his House biography, he lives in Manchester, New Jersey, with his wife, Marie.

record.text: Authored the Victims of Trafficking and Violence Protection Act of 2000 (P.L. 106-386), the first comprehensive federal law against human trafficking, and its subsequent reauthorizations in 2003, 2005, and 2018 (the Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Prevention and Protection Reauthorization Act).
Authored the International Megan's Law of 2016 (P.L. 114-119), which requires notification when registered sex offenders travel internationally.

Authored multiple enacted autism research laws, including the Autism CARES Act of 2024 (P.L. 118-180), the Autism CARES Act of 2019 (P.L. 116-60), and the Combating Autism Reauthorization Act of 2011 (P.L. 112-32).

Authored the Torture Victims Relief Act of 1998 (P.L. 105-320) and its reauthorizations, funding treatment centers for torture survivors, and the Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Anti-Semitism Act (P.L. 116-326).

Authored several enacted veterans-benefits laws, including the Veterans Education and Benefits Expansion Act (P.L. 107-103), the Homeless Veterans Comprehensive Assistance Act (P.L. 107-95), and a 2025 law (P.L. 119-35) naming the Toms River VA clinic the Leonard G. 'Bud' Lomell VA Clinic.
Chairs the House Committee on Foreign Affairs for the 119th Congress (2025–2026); previously chaired its Africa, Global Health, and Human Rights subcommittee across several Congresses.

candidates.name: Rachel Peace
candidates.ballotNote: Won a two-candidate June 2 Democratic primary with 72.8% of the vote

summary.text: Rachel Peace is a communications consultant from the Jersey Shore who founded Hyperfocused Communications in 2022 and says she is a single mother. She is the Democratic nominee for NJ-4, having advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary, and has not previously held elected office. She is campaigning on healthcare access and affordability, childcare, and campaign-finance reform.

background.text: Says she was born and raised at the Jersey Shore; graduated from Brick Township Memorial High School, where she describes her theatrical roots as beginning.
Earned a B.A. in Public Relations, with minors in Drama and Sociology, from Hofstra University in 2014.

Describes early jobs as a certified recreational soccer referee from age 12, minimum-wage work at Wendy's and pizza parlors, and babysitting and daycare work; during college she worked on-campus security and event jobs and held internships, and graduated with a job lined up in public relations.
Earlier in her career worked on NYC Broadway Week, according to her campaign survey.
Founded Hyperfocused Communications in 2022, offering media relations and content marketing to founders, nonprofits, and startups.
Says she has contributed to efforts to curb pollution and protect open spaces, and describes herself as a public servant rather than a politician.
Says she and her five-year-old son are recipients of NJ FamilyCare, the state's low-cost health coverage program.

priorities.text: Supports guaranteed healthcare coverage for all Americans, citing her own family's reliance on NJ FamilyCare and pointing to Commonwealth Fund data on U.S. healthcare outcomes.
Supports guaranteed pre-K starting at age three for all families who want it and 12 weeks of paid parental leave after childbirth.
Says she will cosponsor legislation on her first day in Congress calling for a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United v. FEC.
priorities.quote: On my first day in Congress, I'll cosponsor legislation calling for a constitutional amendment to undo the Supreme Court's disastrous ruling in Citizens United v. FEC.

positions.summary: Supports guaranteed healthcare coverage for all Americans, saying the U.S. is one of the only developed nations without it.
Supports universal pre-K beginning at age three and says childcare costs more than a mortgage for many families.
Supports new environmental legislation to protect the Jersey Shore from coastal flooding and severe storms, and wants oil and gas companies to help pay for climate damage.
positions.quote: Let's make polluters pay: big Oil and Gas have created the problem - they should use their record profits to solve it.
